Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The change affects posted T/H words.

Good checks:

- The tests check stable numbers after an add, import, delete, and legacy project load.
- The tests check undo, redo, and number conflicts on one machine.
- The PR has its decision record and `Process change: yes` line. It does not change `PROCESS_VERSION`.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs:204`: Keep the microARC wrap fixture consistent with its committed golden. The new allocation changes 11 tool-number lines, including comments. `EM 1/4 3FL` changes from T2/H2 to T1/H1. `EM 1/8 2FL` changes from T3/H3 to T2/H2. `BN 1/8` changes from T1/H1 to T3/H3. The fixture adds the ball tool at `crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs:242`. Give that fixture explicit stable numbers that match its committed golden. The golden is `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`. I compared the output with and without the `AddTool::apply` change. Those outputs differ only on these 11 lines. The mutation restores the committed T/H sequence. Thus, this PR adds a deterministic golden mismatch beyond the Linux failure in #2483.
2. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings.rs:334`: Add before and after screenshots to the PR body. Show the tool-number editor and the new add status. The body currently has no screenshots. Store the images only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Link them from the body.

Local results:

- The trial merge with `upstream/main` at `60739b03592eb831c850433a62804a13dd7dad2a` succeeded.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 92 steps passed in 18.8 minutes. The suites recorded 2,359 passed tests and 18 ignored tests. The UI suites ran from `crates/ui`. No pixel snapshot lane ran.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with no warnings.
- I disabled the inherited sccache wrapper after the first planner call stalled. Cargo then ran normally. No GitHub runner ran.
- The separate `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a` test failed with this existing Linux error:

```text
line count 3246 != 3245; regenerate intentional changes with WRITE_GOLDEN=1
```

Issue #2483 tracks that line-count failure. Both allocation variants produce 3,246 lines. Their T/H difference is separate, as finding 1 describes. I used temporary golden generation to inspect the output. I restored the golden after each check. The PR changes no NC or CL golden files. I did not run the full batch gate.

Mutation checks:

| Mutation | Test | Mutated code | Restored code |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AddTool::apply`: set `number: None` | `tool_numbers::adding_an_earlier_sorting_tool_keeps_posted_t_and_h_words` | FAIL: existing tool numbers change | PASS |
| `ImportTools::apply`, `Step::Add`: set `number: None` | `tool_import_modes::update_adds_unmatched_and_skips_identical_in_one_undo` | FAIL: `None` differs from `Some(1)` | PASS |

All mutation source files and generated golden changes were restored. No review evidence was committed or pushed.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f1ed9b6e7aa1a4ea39a8ca14047c3d0ce11a47e8 -->
**Verdict: merge-ready**

No blockers.

**Checked**
- `AddTool::new` and `ImportTools::with_options` take the lowest unused number through `tool_numbers::next_free` / `next_free_from`. The import reserves each number in the batch, so two new tools cannot get the same `T` word. When no number is free, the command is refused by name. It does not wrap.
- `ElectrodeFromFaces` calls `AddTool::new` (`commands/electrode.rs:59`), so it gets a number too. The UI calls `AddTool::with_holder` and MCP `add_tool` calls it too. All add paths use the same command.
- Undo and redo: the number is fixed when the command is created. `DeleteTool` and `ChangeTool` keep the stored number. `SetToolNumber` writes `prev` back on undo. The UI and MCP tests pin this.
- Legacy load: `freeze_legacy_tool_numbers` (`project/apply.rs:957`) sorts by `String::cmp`. `model::named_entities` (`model.rs:140`) uses the same order, and the freeze counts numbered tools too.
